base_retrieval.note: Task 3.5 selected dense-only retrieval (RRF hybrid was practically tied with dense and dense-only was preferred as the simpler architecture) - reranking operates on the frozen Qwen dense-only candidate pool, not the sparse or hybrid stream.

phase3_6_config.candidate_grid_decision: PROJECT_EXECUTION.md Task 3.6 names no specific reranker model (only 'a small serving candidate' + an optional larger quality ceiling) - a materially ambiguous contract per the Task 3.99 controlled-execution-loop's own LOOP STEP 1 rule. User-approved candidate grid (2026-09-12): cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2 only. The optional larger-quality-ceiling comparison is explicitly deferred, not attempted in this round.

reranker.note: Revision pinned from the installed sentence-transformers 6.0.0's own resolved huggingface_hub cache ref at pilot time - never 'main'. Score direction (higher=more relevant, raw unbounded logit, no sigmoid applied) verified empirically before formal code was written: a clearly relevant pair scored ~9.1, a mismatched pair ~-7.3.

phase3_6_config.candidate_set_recall_note: Reranking reorders the fixed 50-chunk dense candidate pool only - it can never change which chunks are in that pool. doc_recall@50 is therefore mathematically identical before and after reranking (verified at run time via src.eval.phase3_rerank.assert_candidate_set_recall_unchanged) and is reported for continuity, never claimed as an improvement.
phase3_6_config.metric_definitions: doc_recall@10/@50 (continuity metrics, unchanged by reranking) via the same Task 2.6 granularity-agnostic functions used since Task 3.4; doc_mrr, doc_ndcg@10 (rank10-based, Task 2.6 + Task 3.1's document_relevances_at_k); doc_precision_at_5 (new Task 3.6 metric, src.eval.metrics.precision_at_k, over the same document_relevances_at_k(...,k=5) binary relevance vector - one hit maximum per document, never a new dedup rule); doc_recall_at_5 (hit@5, Task 2.6's hit_at_k). PROJECT_EXECUTION.md's own Task 3.6 'Primary metrics' list (MRR, nDCG@10, Precision@5, Recall@5).
phase3_6_config.selection_rule: src.eval.phase3_rerank.select_rerank_configuration: priority order doc_mrr > doc_ndcg@10 > doc_precision_at_5 > doc_recall_at_5 against the no-rerank (dense-only) baseline. Practical tie: Recall@5 hit delta <= 1 out of 89 AND paired MRR/nDCG@10 95% bootstrap CIs both include 0 -> prefer no_rerank (simpler, avoids the reranker's extra query-time model call). A win on one ranking metric with a credible (95% CI entirely below 0) regression on another is flagged for a user decision, never auto-resolved. A negative result (no_rerank remains selected) is a fully valid Task 3.6 outcome, exactly as Task 3.5 established for hybrid fusion.

selection.rationale: reranking does not improve any ranking metric over no-rerank on the frozen priority order.

ablation_row.notes: Task 3.6: cross-encoder rerank (cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2) over Task 3.5-selected dense-only candidate pool (base_k=50). Selection: reranking does not improve any ranking metric over no-rerank on the frozen priority order.

limitations: Evaluated only over the frozen Task 3.1 89-question DEV/evaluable-subset (4.9% of full DEV).
N=89 is small; bootstrap CIs govern which reranked-vs-no-rerank differences are credible.
Only cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2 was benchmarked - the roadmap's optional larger quality-ceiling comparison was explicitly deferred, not attempted in this round.
doc_recall@50 is mathematically identical before/after reranking (same candidate set, only reordered) - never claimed as an improvement.
chunk_recall@10, chunk_mrr, faithfulness, citation_grounding, and generation metrics remain N/A.
